title: Train the annealer
summary: One auto-anatomist trial: trains while the mask input is annealed away, one array task a trial.
does: One trial of the auto-anatomist screen (#483): the anneal schedule (lambda-then-w, joint, w-first, or fixed, the null), the objective (the oracle's landmarks, or the mask channels themselves), the naming term, the calibration of the spreads, the epochs, whole phantoms a batch and the seed. Each trial is one task of a GPU array (grid/autoanatomist.sbatch there: 8 CPUs, 64 GB, 12 h). A plan's epochs are at most 1000 and its batch at most 64; objective=mask needs naming off and calibrate none.

inputs.name: model
inputs.what: The auto-anatomist network, built for split CT crops.

outputs.name: checkpoint
outputs.what: The trial's weights and its curve.

params.name: schedule
params.what: how lambda's and w's ramps are placed; fixed is the null

params.name: objective
params.what: what the decoder is trained to give

params.name: naming
params.what: whether the naming term is in the loss

params.name: epochs
params.what: epochs a trial; a plan takes at most 1000

params.name: batch
params.what: whole phantoms a batch; a plan takes at most 64

params.name: seed
params.what: the network's initialisation and the session's draws

nondeterminism: JAX on a GPU may differ in its last bits between runs; each trial records its words and their digest.

generic.why: It trains on 3-D CT crops (#483); 2-D frames would need a 2-D network and crops of their own.

today.note: Built on the unmerged pull request #483 (flows/autoanatomist.py and grid/screens/ on its branch); nothing on main runs it until that pull request merges.
